thread:
infra-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert — repeated OOMs on pod kv-paged-alloc-23 in prod-gpupool-3. CUDA OOM + container restart loop detected. Logs attached: short excerpt below.

infra-bot: `ERROR: CUDA out of memory. cuMemAlloc failed at allocator.cc:124`

oncall-jane: seeing it, pinging eng-sre. I'll start triage.

alex: confirmed OOMs correlate with high paged-attn allocations. KV-cache size climbing steady; fragmentation looks like slow creep, not one-off spike.

sarah: copying logs, here's the tail:
```
[2026-03-16T22:08:12Z] kv-paged-alloc: alloc(12MB) -> slab 0x7f2b... failed: OOM
[2026-03-16T22:08:12Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-16T22:08:13Z] container restart
```

oncall-jane: estimated impact? ops-ryan?

ops-ryan: telemetry shows ~4.8% 5xx rate increase for /v1/generate in us-west1 over last 12m, tail latency up. One enterprise tenant (acme-corp) reported errors on chat endpoints. No billing spikes.

miguel: likely KV page fragmentation + slow non-reclaiming of orphaned slots. Quick mitigations: reduce per-request KV retention, force a small eviction, and cordon node if unstable.

alex: agree. Steps I can run now: 1) toggle emergency eviction flag, 2) flush non-critical prefixes, 3) drain node if restarts persist.

sarah: running eviction toggle and a targeted flush for long-lived prefixes we identified. Posting commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/kv-service KV_EVICT_RATIO=0.65
curl -X POST "https://admin.prod.internal/cache/flush?prefix=kv://model/large/beam" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" 
# if restarts continue:
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=60
```

oncall-jane: do we have safe fallback model variants? Can we route traffic to smaller model to reduce KV pressure?

miguel: yes — route policy 'fallback-small' exists. We can failover canary 5% traffic to model-small for affected routes. That reduces KV working set.

eng-sre-bot: runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/incidents/paged-kv-frag. Recommended: set eviction, enable compact-mode, and schedule compaction job. Escalate to infra if node flaps persist.

alex: eviction toggle applied, flush returned 204. Observing memory usage dropping on pod, restarts stopped for now.

ops-ryan: 5xx rate down to +1.2% above baseline. Customer reported immediate improvement.

oncall-jane: marking this as sev2 (customer-visible errors, limited scope). I'll keep watch for 30m, then coordinate a controlled compaction and a follow-up postmortem if this reoccurs.

sarah: leaving a note in the incident channel and tagging oncall-next: @oncall-next please pick up at 23:15 UTC. Summary: CUDA OOMs from KV-paged allocator caused pod restarts due to fragmentation/slow leak. Mitigation: emergency eviction + prefix flush, minor traffic canary to model-small, drained gpu-node-23 if needed.

oncall-jane: handoff to @oncall-next: please verify node stability, run the compaction job during low traffic window, and check for any lingering orphaned KV slots (metric: kv.page.orphans). I'll update the ticket with commands we ran. :white_check_mark:

eng-sre-bot: noting follow-ups: schedule compaction job, add telemetry for kv.page.fragmentation_ratio, review allocator heuristics for slow leak patterns.

oncall-jane: closing thread for live mitigation — reopen if OOMs return. :handshake:
